sources.title: Models | Aion Labs Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27: the exact Aion 3.0 entry identifies a collaborative system of multiple specialized GLM-family models and release 2026-05-05. It names no specific GLM base, component inventory, nominal size, active count or structural modification. The explicitly named DeepSeek V3.2 variant elsewhere on the page is Aion 2.0, not Aion 3.0.

sources.title: Aion Labs public models API
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27: exact ID aion-labs/aion-3.0 repeats the GLM-family collaborative-system description with context_length 131072, text-to-text modality, reasoning true and tool_calls true. Neither the data record nor its models duplicate supplies parameter counts, named GLM versions, component counts or routing/activation details.

sources.title: API Reference | Aion Labs Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27: the API reference defines release dates, model capability metadata and reasoning-effort settings. Its model-response schema has no total or active parameter specifications; Aion 3.0 supports none, low, medium, high and max reasoning effort, default medium.

sources.title: Terms of Service | Aion Labs
sources.evidence: Current terms identify the Aion Labs brand with Deep Forge sp. z o.o. Section 6 grants model usage through the service but no other model rights; this is an API service agreement, not a released-weight license.

sources.title: Aion Labs models on Hugging Face
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27: official Aion Labs organization links to aionlabs.ai and aionlabsai on GitHub; its two listed models remain Aion-RP-Llama-3.1-8B and its GGUF variant. No Aion 3.0 card, configuration or named-base disclosure appears in that listing.

sources.title: Aion-3.0 | OpenRouter
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27: the exact serving-platform page repeats the GLM-family collaborative multi-model description without named component versions or total/active counts. Its July 7, 2026 release label still conflicts with the original developer date. Used as corroboration and a discovery lead, not as a source of inherited GLM counts.

sources.title: Models.dev Aion 3.0 record
sources.evidence: Baseline-linked catalog entry was accessed as a discovery lead; primary developer documentation and API were separately inspected.

sources.title: Aion Labs GitHub profile
sources.evidence: Checked 2026-10-27 through the GitHub link on the official Hugging Face organization. The profile lists zero public repositories and no Aion 3.0 technical report, configuration or model card. This search produced no additional parameter or named-base evidence.

name.note: Use developer spelling after removing its display-name vendor prefix.

developer.note: Developer brand is Aion Labs; legal service operator is Deep Forge sp. z o.o.

family.note: GLM lineage is explicit; the precise component versions are unspecified.

release_date.note: Original developer explicitly reports May 5. OpenRouter reports July 7; retain the developer date and record the platform discrepancy.

open_weights.note: API access is verified, but the inspected primary pages do not explicitly classify this exact system as closed. No Aion 3.0 weights/card were found in the official Hugging Face listing; absence alone does not prove non-release.

license.note: No model-weight license was identified. Service terms are not evidence of a separately distributed checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh primary-source and exact-model searches found no nominal total count or explicit relationship to a named GLM base. Only family-level lineage is disclosed, so neither a component count nor a system total can be inherited; the gap is model identity, not an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: No nominal active count or named component with a documented active count is disclosed. Multiple models contribute to each response, but the activation schedule is unspecified; family-level lineage does not establish per-token or per-response active parameters.

architecture.note: Verified at system level: several specialized models contribute to responses. Neural-layer architecture, component count, and dense/MoE composition remain undisclosed; this label does not assert those details.

context_window.note: Exact context_length in the live developer API, in tokens.

modalities.note: The exact API record declares text-to-text modality.

reasoning.note: Exact capability flag is true; reasoning can be disabled through reasoning_effort=none.

tool_call.note: Exact capability flag tool_calls is true, with its API semantics documented.

description.value: GLM-based multi-model system for narrative generation, with collaborative response generation, reasoning, and tool calling.
description.note: Replace the generic analytical-use description with the documented system and intended narrative use; omit unsupported quality comparisons.

patch.name: Aion 3.0
patch.description: GLM-based multi-model system for narrative generation, with collaborative response generation, reasoning, and tool calling.
patch.notes: GLM-family collaborative multi-model system; specific component models and total/active parameter counts are undisclosed. Family-level lineage does not identify a base from which to inherit nominal counts. No Aion 3.0 weight release or weight license was verified. Developer release date is 2026-05-05; OpenRouter labels 2026-07-07.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit on 2026-10-27 retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening developer documentation, live API, official Hugging Face and GitHub profiles, and the OpenRouter listing, plus searches for exact-model counts and named GLM bases. No nominal specification or named-base relationship was found; the documented multi-model structure does not disclose component identity or activation. Explicit null parameter patches preserve that uncertainty. Other audited fields and prior corrections are unchanged.
